# Generated files

Everything the scripts generate lives in `state/` — gitignored as a whole (it contains keys). See [`examples/`](../examples/) for annotated samples.

| File | What | Secret? |
|---|---|---|
| `state/wg.key` | your WireGuard private key | **yes** |
| `state/stunmesh0.conf` | WireGuard config, written by setup once the peer key is provided | **yes** (holds the private key) |
| `state/config.yaml` | stunmesh-go config, generated by start if absent | no |
| `state/settings.env` | node identity — tunnel IPs + peer public key + peer SSH user + selected DHT endpoint; read as a plain `KEY=VALUE` list | no |
| `state/peers.d/<name>.env` | one file per extra peer for the hub use-case (`KEY` / `IP` / `SSH_USER`); absent on a plain 2-node setup. See [hub.md](hub.md) | no (public keys only) |
| `state/ssh.conf` | Host alias block, written by `make ssh-setup` | no |
| `state/stunmesh-go` | upstream release binary, plus `stunmesh.log` / `stunmesh.pid` at runtime | no |

`stunmesh0.conf`, `config.yaml`, and `settings.env` are all fine to hand-edit — editing one `settings.env` line is a valid alternative to re-running setup. Delete any generated file to get a fresh one.

`start` never overwrites an existing `config.yaml`; it only refreshes the interface-name line (the macOS `utunX` changes per boot) and the selected DHT `endpoint:` line, and leaves a custom endpoint you set by hand untouched. See [how-it-works.md](how-it-works.md).
